newsitem.title: ITALY: US Navy rescues 20 Albanians at sea for five days.
newsitem.headline: US Navy rescues 20 Albanians at sea for five days.

text.p: Twenty Albanians who had drifted in a boat in the Adriatic Sea for five days -- three of them without food and water -- in a desperate attempt to flee to Italy, have been rescued by the U.S. Navy.

A statement from a U.S. marine task force in the Adriatic said the 20, all men, abandoned their powerless, leaking, 25-foot (eight-metre) vessel, when a rescue boat from the cruiser Leyte Gulf pulled alongside late on Monday.
"The vessel's passengers began jumping into the sea, leaving their personal belongings behind, to swim towards Leyte Gulf," the statement, sent to Reuters in Rome on Tuesday, said.
"The Albanian refugees were at sea for five days, three of them without food or fresh water. Of the 20 passengers, three were severely dehydrated and required medical assistance."
The group, spotted by a U.S. Navy Sea Hawk helicopter, were being transferred to the marine force command ship USS Nassau and then to Brindisi, southeast Italy.
The Nassau, in command of the U.S. operation to evacuate American nationals from Albania's unrest, already has 85 Albanians on board following their resce from two vessels in distress on Sunday.

Some 8,000 Albanians have fled to Italy in the past several days in a ramshackle flotilla of rusting boats. Many recent arrivals said they paid racketeers in the port of Durres for a passage to Italy.
